steps.body: The **conjugate** of a + bi is a − bi — same real part, flipped imaginary sign. Multiply a number by its conjugate and the i vanishes: (a + bi)(a − bi) = **a² + b²**, always a real number. For 3 + 2i: (3 + 2i)(3 − 2i) = 9 + 4 = 13.
A conjugate kills the imaginary part.

widget.prompt: w = 2 − 3i. Find the z whose product z × w is real: land it on 13.
widget.successFeedback: z = 2 + 3i, the conjugate of w. Their product is 2² + 3² = 13 — a real number, every time, with the imaginary parts cancelling exactly. THAT is why dividing complex numbers multiplies top and bottom by the conjugate: it is the move that clears i out of the denominator.
widget.realFeedback: The product is not landing on 13. Try the mirror image of w across the real axis.
widget.imagFeedback: The real part is right, but there is still an imaginary part left. Only the exact conjugate cancels it completely.

predict.prompt: w = 2 − 3i. Which z makes the product z × w purely REAL?

options.label: Any z on the real axis

predict.reveal: A number times its conjugate is |w|²: (2 + 3i)(2 − 3i) = 4 + 9 = 13 — the imaginary parts cancel in equal and opposite pairs. That cancellation is the entire engine of complex division.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents conjugate.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for conjugate must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines conjugate.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: That real product is the key to **division**: to divide by a complex number, multiply top and bottom by the **bottom's conjugate**. Example: (3 + i)/(1 − i). Multiply by (1 + i)/(1 + i): bottom becomes 1 + 1 = 2, top becomes (3 + i)(1 + i) = 2 + 4i, so the answer is **1 + 2i**.

explanationVariants: Keep the real part, flip only the imaginary sign: −2 + 7i ↦ −2 − 7i.
The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi — one sign changes, the b's sign.

options.label: −2 − 7i
options.feedback: Right — only the imaginary sign flips.

options.label: 2 − 7i
options.feedback: That flipped BOTH signs — the real part stays −2.

options.label: 2 + 7i
options.feedback: That flipped the REAL sign — the conjugate flips only the imaginary one: −2 − 7i.

options.label: 7 − 2i
options.feedback: That swapped the parts — conjugation keeps each part in place and flips b's sign.

widget.prompt: To divide by 1 − i, multiply by its conjugate 1 + i. What real number is (1 − i)(1 + i)?

commonErrors.feedback: 1 − 1 subtracts — the conjugate product ADDS the squares: 1² + 1² = 2.
1 is only a² — add b² = 1 as well: 2.

widget.fallbackFeedback: a² + b² = 1 + 1 = 2 — a clean real denominator.

explanationVariants: Top: (3 + i)(1 + i) = 3 + 3i + i + i² = 2 + 4i; bottom: 2. Result (2 + 4i)/2 = 1 + 2i.
After multiplying by (1 + i)/(1 + i), divide BOTH parts of 2 + 4i by 2.

options.label: 2 + 4i
options.feedback: That's the numerator before the final step — divide both parts by the denominator 2.

options.label: 3 − i
options.feedback: You can't just cancel pieces across a complex fraction — multiply top AND bottom by the conjugate 1 + i.

options.label: 1 − 2i
options.feedback: Sign slip in the numerator: (3 + i)(1 + i) has +4i, giving 1 + 2i.

commonErrors.feedback: 25 − 4 subtracts — the pattern is a² PLUS b²: 25 + 4 = 29.
25 is only 5² — the imaginary coefficient adds its square: + 4 = 29.

explanationVariants: Multiply by (1 − i)/(1 − i): bottom 2, top (4 + 2i)(1 − i) = 4 − 4i + 2i + 2 = 6 − 2i; result 3 − i, real part 3.

widget.prompt: Simplify (4 + 2i)/(1 + i). What is the REAL part of the result?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 is the numerator's real part BEFORE dividing by the denominator 2: 6/2 = 3.
The 4 can't pass through untouched — multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 1 − i first, then divide by 2.

hints: The bottom is 1 + i — multiply top and bottom by its conjugate, 1 − i.
Divide both parts by 2: 3 − i — the real part is 3.

steps.body: Conjugates erase i: multiply by them to divide.
takeaways: Conjugate of a + bi is a − bi — flip only the imaginary sign.
(a + bi)(a − bi) = a² + b², always real, never negative.
To divide: multiply top and bottom by the bottom's conjugate, then split the parts.

concept.body: The conjugate flips ONLY the sign on the i-term: 4 + 3i becomes 4 − 3i.

explanationVariants: a + bi ↦ a − bi with a = 4, b = 3.

options.label: 4 − 3i
options.feedback: Right — only the imaginary sign flips.

options.label: −4 + 3i
options.feedback: The REAL sign flipped — it should stay 4: the conjugate is 4 − 3i.

options.label: −4 − 3i
options.feedback: Both signs flipped — conjugation changes only the i-term's sign.

options.label: 3 − 4i
options.feedback: The parts swapped places — each part stays put; only the i-sign flips.
